questions.question: Day 15 Practice (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)): When talking about inquiring about doctor appointment (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My colleague'?

options.a: I am inquiring about doctor appointment right now.
options.b: Doctor meeting wanted for fever.
options.c: Doctor meeting wanted for fever. yesterday
options.d: I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I need to consult a doctor regarding a mild fever.".

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'circle back'?

options.a: Return to a topic later for follow-up.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'circle back' means: return to a topic later for follow-up. Example: "Let us circle back to the timeline discussion."

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'drop by'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: Visit someone informally for a short time.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'drop by' means: visit someone informally for a short time. Example: "Feel free to drop by our home this evening."

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'call off'?

options.b: Cancel a planned event or meeting.

options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'call off' means: cancel a planned event or meeting. Example: "They had to call off the afternoon presentation."

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'reach out to'?

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 1 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "రేపటి మీటింగ్ 3 గంటలకు రీషెడ్యూల్ చేయవచ్చా?"
(Literal attempt: "Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.c: Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.d: Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?"

Use 'Could we reschedule...' for polite professional requests.

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 2 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.c: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.d: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:

(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.
options.c: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.d: First problem root cause finding wanted.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 4 (Mergers & Acquisition Synergies (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.d: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.
